answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy makes identity cost capital, not a keypair. Each registration posts its own bond, locked and slashable, so one operator signing a thousand addresses must fund a thousand bonds and absorb slashing of the whole opal of pooled stake if the cluster misbehaves. Attacker outlay grows linearly per head, while honest work costs one stake. Merit persists on the ridge of steady reputation and paid weight cannot buy it. One old sonnet read aloud a thousand times pays again each time; the same words cannot claim a new voice.
